comparison: Perfect agreement on barrier mechanism (C117-C131). Both evaluations support the structural characterization of inner and outer barriers, contact area calculations, and the conclusion about differential stability. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings without challenge.

Strong agreement on the mechanistic model (C172-C181, C190-C191). Both support the integration of structural and thermodynamic data into the transport mechanism. OpenEval explicitly validates the stepped-binding model while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic conclusions about coupled transport without objection.

Complete agreement on Na+ binding site characterization (C88-C97, C99, C193-C194). Both evaluations support the structural identification, functional validation through mutagenesis, and MD simulation results. Neither raises concerns about conformation-independent Na+ binding.

Significant disagreement on HDX-MS interpretation (C142-C163, C197-C205). OpenEval supports the data as measuring conformational dynamics with appropriate statistical analysis. Peer Reviewer 1 challenges this interpretation, arguing the experiment measures accessibility rather than dynamics, and notes the comparison is between a trapped state and an ensemble, making differential dynamics 'obvious' rather than informative.

Agreement on ITC binding data and negative cooperativity (C54-C63). Both evaluations support the thermodynamic measurements showing differential effects on sugar versus Na+ binding. OpenEval provides detailed validation of internal consistency while peer reviewers accept the biophysical measurements without challenge.

Agreement on structural comparison and sugar-binding pocket disruption (C100-C108). Both support the correlation between structural changes and reduced sugar affinity. OpenEval validates the inference about sugar-releasing conformation while peer reviewers implicitly accept the mechanistic interpretation.

Complete agreement on cryoEM structure determination (C65-C76). Both evaluations support the resolution, model quality, and structural analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly praise overcoming technical challenges while OpenEval validates methodological soundness and conformational selectivity conclusions.

Agreement on core mechanistic conclusions (C221-C222). Both support the mobile barrier mechanism and differential regulation of sugar versus Na+ binding. OpenEval validates these as well-supported major conclusions while peer reviewers describe the study as important without challenging the mechanism.

Agreement on linking structural observations to functional consequences (C132-C137, C134-C137). Both support the connection between conformational changes and measured affinity changes. OpenEval validates the mechanistic inference while peer reviewers accept the structural-functional correlation.

Agreement on nanobody functional mimicry of EIIAGlc (C214-C218, C215-C218, C223). Both support the conformation-selective properties and functional equivalence. Peer Reviewer 1 specifically praises the nanobody approach while OpenEval validates the functional data and ternary complex isolation.

Agreement on conceptual advance and mechanistic model (C190-C191 overlap with R9's C172-C181). Both support the extension of single-site model and implications for substrate accumulation. OpenEval validates the conceptual contribution while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic understanding.

Partial overlap on nanobody engineering and binding characterization (C45-C53 from OpenEval, C48-C49 shared with peer R2). OpenEval validates the CDR grafting and functional assays while peer reviewers accept the binding measurements as part of broader biophysical evidence.

Agreement on differential cation versus sugar binding behavior (C192-C196 from OpenEval, C193-C194 shared). Both support conformation-independent Na+ binding. OpenEval validates MD simulations and speculative hypotheses while peer reviewers accept the differential binding without challenge.

Disagreement on HDX-MS interpretation in conformational context (C200-C204 from OpenEval overlap with R6's broader HDX critique). OpenEval supports the interpretation of protection patterns reflecting conformational ensembles. Peer Reviewer 1 questions whether HDX differences truly reveal conformational transitions versus accessibility in trapped versus ensemble states.

Disagreement on allosteric mechanism from HDX-MS (C205-C213 from OpenEval, C205 shared). OpenEval supports the integration of HDX, structural, and mutagenesis data for allosteric model. Peer Reviewer 1's critique of HDX interpretation as measuring accessibility rather than dynamics undermines this mechanistic proposal.

OpenEval supports structural comparison and rocker-switch mechanism (C110-C116) with quantitative rmsd values and domain-specific alignments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific structural comparison claims.

OpenEval supports integration of HDX-MS dynamics with structural features (C164-C169), including spatial clustering and linkage between binding and barrier residues. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R6 challenges broader HDX interpretation.
